key_insight: The paper shows that a rule-based Bernoulli Naive Bayes system with χ²-guided binning can make medical predictions that stay interpretable while still performing well.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians and health systems use AI models that explain their thresholds and risk estimates more clearly than black-box methods.
method: χ²-guided binarization converts continuous inputs into clinically readable thresholds.
Bernoulli Naive Bayes then classifies using those binary rules.
Calibration was checked and improved with leakage-safe cross-validation and beta calibration.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark datasets, the model reported AUCs of 0.800 for Pima Indians Diabetes, 0.984 for Wisconsin Breast Cancer, and 0.919 for Heart Failure Prediction, with calibration analysis also performed.
watch_item: Thresholds are learned from training data, so their stability and generalizability may vary across new populations or settings.
paper_title: A Transportable Threshold-Based Framework for Interpretable Classification of Medical Data
